- If sentiment is negative or shows recent downward momentum, reduce forecast slope or shift mean downward to avoid over-optimism.  
- If forecast shows strong upward trend after a recent spike, cap growth or introduce early mean reversion to prevent overshoot.  
- When true outcome diverges sharply from forecast (especially after a spike), assume model overreacted and adjust downward by 5–15% of forecast range.  
- If sentiment is positive and forecast is flat or declining, consider upward bias correction — especially if recent history shows volatility or reversal.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is consistently above true outcome by >10% over 3–5 days, apply downward bias correction to avoid overestimating upward momentum.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple 0.00 or neutral entries, assume low confidence — reduce forecast volatility and avoid sharp directional moves.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion after a spike, model should reflect this by reducing forecast slope or introducing a “reversion zone” near prior 10–15 day average.
